text:
tanya: Hey all, first week and hitting a blocker. I can SSH into bastion but `docker pull internal.registry.redwood:5000/myorg/tool:latest` just hangs when I'm on corporate VPN (split-tunnel enabled). If I disconnect VPN it works but then I lose access to other internal stuff. Anyone know a clean workaround?

ron: Welcome Tanya! This is usually the split-tunnel routing — Docker daemon traffic doesn't get routed through the user VPN interface by default. Two quick checks: 1) can you curl the registry from your host? 2) can you reach the registry from the bastion?

tanya: `curl -v http://internal.registry.redwood:5000/v2/` -> times out. From bastion `curl http://internal.registry.redwood:5000/v2/` -> 200 OK.

maya: Confirms it's a host routing issue. Short-term hack: use an SSH local forward: `ssh -L 5000:internal.registry.redwood:5000 ec2-user@bastion.redwood` and then `docker pull localhost:5000/myorg/tool:latest`. That avoids changing daemon proxy.

ron: Another option on macOS with Docker Desktop: use `docker run --rm --network host` won't work because Desktop doesn't expose host network. Instead, try `docker run --rm curlimages/curl curl -v http://host.docker.internal:5000/v2/` to verify container can reach mapped host endpoint.

tanya: Tried `ssh -L` and docker pull works. Thanks! For the long run, what's the right ticket to get registry routed via VPN so new hires don't need this?

maya: File a request with the network team to add a route for the registry subnet to the VPN tunnel (include registry FQDN + ip). If network says no (policy), infra can add an authenticated reverse-proxy in the DMZ that forwards to the registry.

infra-bot: Network request created: NET-2441 (maya -> network).

ron: FYI if you prefer not to forward ports, `ssh -D` socks proxy also works for user-space tools: `ssh -D 1080 ec2-user@bastion.redwood` then `export ALL_PROXY=socks5h://localhost:1080` and test with `curl`. But Docker daemon won't use ALL_PROXY unless configured for the daemon.

maya: If infra wants to configure Docker daemon proxy on mac/linux, the approaches are: systemd drop-in with environment vars or Docker Desktop -> Preferences -> Resources -> Proxies (mac). For Linux servers: create `/etc/systemd/system/docker.service.d/http-proxy.conf` with `Environment=HTTP_PROXY=...` and `systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart docker`.

tanya: Noted. One more weirdness: my `docker login` failed with x509: certificate signed by unknown authority when I used the forwarded localhost:5000. Any tips?

ron: That means registry uses internal CA. Two fixes: 1) add the internal CA cert to your system's trust store (mac: Keychain; linux: /etc/ssl/certs) and restart Docker; 2) set up the ssh tunnel to use the registry's hostname (ssh -L 5000:internal.registry.redwood:5000 ...) and use `docker pull internal.registry.redwood:5000/...` so TLS hostname matches cert.

maya: Good call. If you plan to keep the tunnel, use the real hostname in TLS to avoid cert issues.

devops-bot: Onboarding note added: WORKAROUND-REGISTRY-TUNNEL (maya)

infra-bot: NET-2441 assigned to @network-team.

maya: I'll follow up on the ticket and loop you in, Tanya. Meanwhile add the tunnel command to your onboarding checklist.

tanya: Thanks everyone 389 Saved me from a whole morning of pain!
